```md design/README.md
# codx-junior — Design Documentation

Corporate image and UI/UX foundation for **codx-junior**, derived from an audit of the
shipping product (`client/` — project `codx-junior-ui`).

> **Status:** v0.1 — *baseline definition*. Everything here describes either
> (a) what the product does **today**, verified in code, or (b) a **decision
> proposal** to close a gap. Each statement is labelled so the two never get
> confused.

> **Start here — [`playbook/index.html`](playbook/index.html).** The whole design system on
> one self-contained page: live component specimens, dark/light toggle, print-ready layout.
> Hand it to any developer before they write UI code.

---

## Why this folder exists

codx-junior grew feature-first: 400+ Vue components, several parallel shells
(desktop dockview, mobile app shell, company shell, solopreneur shell) and three
different colour palettes that leaked into the codebase over time. The product
works, but it does not yet look like *one company*.

This folder is the single place where the corporate image is defined, so that:

- a new screen can be designed without inventing new colours, spacing or copy;
- a designer and a developer can agree on a spec without a meeting;
- rebrand work (logo, palette, marketing site) has a contract to break *on purpose*.

---

## How to read it

| Folder | Contents | Audience |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `playbook/` | **The playbook** (`index.html`) — this whole folder on one page, with rendered specimens | Developers, new joiners |
| `resources/` | **Official artwork** — `logo.png` (the mark, 267 × 266 PNG + alpha) and `me-and-codx-junior.png` (brand photograph). Embedded by the playbook, taken from here, never re-exported | Everyone |
| `00-audit/` | What the current UI actually is, with file-level evidence | Designers, tech leads |
| `01-brand/` | Brand platform, logo, colour, typography, voice — the *corporate image* | Everyone, marketing included |
| `02-design-system/` | Foundations (space, radius, motion, layering) and component specs | Designers, frontend |
| `03-ux/` | Information architecture, navigation model, accessibility | Designers, PMs, frontend |
| `04-assets/` | Asset production rules: formats, sizes, naming, export | Design, marketing |
| `05-governance/` | Ownership, versioning, review checklist, adoption roadmap | Leads |
| `06-calendar/` | **Feature design** — agenda/calendar manager: deep analysis, clickable prototype, API fixtures. Design only, no code changed | Product, frontend, backend |
| `07-chat-timeline/` | **Feature design** — chat turn timeline (DevTools-style waterfall of a message's processing events) + insights rail. Clickable mockup, design only | Product, frontend, backend |
| `tokens/` | `design-tokens.json` — machine-readable source for the values above | Frontend |

Reading order for a newcomer: **audit → brand platform → colour → typography →
foundations → components → IA**.

---

## Ground rules

1. **The code is the current truth; this folder is the target truth.** When they
   disagree, the documents say which one wins.
2. **No new colour, radius or spacing value without a token.** If a value is
   missing, add a token here first, then use it.
3. **Every doc is versioned with the product**, not separately. See
   `05-governance/design-ops.md`.
4. **Numbers beat adjectives.** "16px, 8px grid, 4.5:1" is a spec; "modern and
   clean" is not.

---

## Source of truth (code references used throughout)

| Concern | File |

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
<title>Mockup — Message header & actions (3 directions)</title>
<!--
  MOCKUP — chat message header + action menu, three directions (A / B / C).
  Single file. No build step. No network. Open directly in a browser.
  Design tokens follow design/01-brand/color-system.md (magenta spectrum on deep blue-slate).
  Every fake boundary is marked with "MOCK:".

  WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR
  The current header (see design/08-message-header/README.md) puts identity, state,
  receipts, reactions and actions on one line at the same visual weight, and hides
  the rest behind a flat 11-item ⋯ menu that drops ON TOP of the turn waterfall.
  Three directions are proposed here; each keeps the waterfall visible while the
  actions are open, which is the one hard requirement.
-->
<style>
  /* ── design tokens (design/01-brand/color-system.md) ─────────────────── */
  :root{
    --bg:            oklch(15% 0.03 240);
    --surface:       oklch(22% 0.04 240);
    --surface-2:     oklch(26% 0.04 240);
    --sunken:        oklch(15% 0.03 240);
    --text:          oklch(96% 0.02 240);
    --text-2:        color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 70%, transparent);
    --text-3:        color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 52%, transparent);
    --border:        color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 11%, transparent);
    --border-soft:   color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 6%, transparent);
    --primary:       oklch(65% 0.30 330);
    --primary-soft:  #FF69B4;
    --secondary:     #8F008F;
    --info:          oklch(75% 0.22 220);
    --success:       oklch(68% 0.28 140);
    --warning:       oklch(82% 0.26 70);
    --error:         oklch(68% 0.32 25);
    --violet:        #7C5CFF;
    --teal:          #14B8A6;
    --r-sm:6px; --r-md:10px; --r-lg:14px; --r-pill:999px;
    --ui: system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",Roboto,sans-serif;
    --mono: "SF Mono",Menlo,Monaco,"Courier New",monospace;
    --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.4), 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.28);
    --fast:150ms;
  }
  *,*::before,*::after{ box-sizing:border-box }
  html,body{ margin:0 }
  body{
    min-height:100vh;
    color:var(--text);
    font:400 14px/1.55 var(--ui);
    background:
      radial-gradient(1100px 520px at 12% -12%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 14%, transparent), transparent 62%),
      radial-gradient(900px 460px at 92% 0%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--info) 10%, transparent), transparent 60%),
      var(--bg);
    -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;
  }
  .mono{ font-family:var(--mono) }
  .i{ width:14px; height:14px; flex:0 0 auto; fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:1.7; stroke-linecap:round; stroke-linejoin:round }
  .i.sm{ width:12px; height:12px }
  .sprite{ position:absolute; width:0; height:0; overflow:hidden }
  .kicker{ font:600 10px/1 var(--ui); letter-spacing:.09em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--text-3) }

  /* ── top bar ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .topbar{
    position:sticky; top:0; z-index:20;
    display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; flex-wrap:wrap;
    padding:10px 20px;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--bg) 88%, transparent);
    backdrop-filter:blur(10px);
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--border-soft);
  }
  .brand{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; min-width:0 }
  .brand-mark{
    width:26px;height:26px;border-radius:8px;flex:0 0 auto;
    background:linear-gradient(140deg, var(--primary), var(--secondary));
    box-shadow:0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 40%, transparent), 0 0 18px color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 35%, transparent);
    display:grid;place-items:center; color:#fff; font:700 12px/1 var(--ui)
  }
  .brand-t{ font:650 14px/1.2 var(--ui) }
  .brand-s{ font-size:11px; color:var(--text-3) }
  .topbar .spacer{ flex:1 }

  /* ── primitives ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .seg{ display:inline-flex; padding:2px; gap:2px; border-radius:9px; background:var(--sunken); border:1px solid var(--border-soft) }
  .seg button{
    display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px;
    height:28px; padding:0 12px; border:0; border-radius:7px;
    background:transparent; color:var(--text-2); font:600 12px/1 var(--ui); cursor:pointer;
    transition:background var(--fast), color var(--fast);
  }
  .seg button:hover{ color:var(--text); background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 6%, transparent) }
  .seg button[aria-pressed="true"]{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 24%, transparent); color:var(--text); box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 40%, transparent) }
  .seg .tag{ font:700 9px/1 var(--ui); padding:2px 4px; border-radius:4px; background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 10%, transparent); color:var(--text-3) }
  .seg button[aria-pressed="true"] .tag{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 45%, transparent); color:#fff }
  .kbd{
    display:inline-grid; place-items:center; min-width:17px; height:17px; padding:0 4px;
    border-radius:4px; border:1px solid var(--border);
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 5%, transparent);
    font:600 10px/1 var(--mono); color:var(--text-3);
  }
  .badge{
    display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:4px; height:18px; padding:0 6px;
    border-radius:var(--r-pill); font:600 10px/1 var(--ui); letter-spacing:.01em;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 8%, transparent); color:var(--text-2);
  }
  .badge.ok{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--success) 18%, transparent); color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--success) 88%, white) }
  .badge.info{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--info) 16%, transparent); color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--info) 85%, white) }
  .badge.warn{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--warning) 18%, transparent); color:var(--warning) }
  .badge .i{ width:10px; height:10px }

  /* ── layout ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .wrap{ max-width:1180px; margin:0 auto; padding:16px 20px 64px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:14px }
  .variant{ display:none; flex-direction:column; gap:14px }
  body[data-variant="a"] #va,
  body[data-variant="b"] #vb,
  body[data-variant="c"] #vc{ display:flex }

  .intro{
    display:grid; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.15fr) minmax(0,1fr); gap:18px;
    background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:var(--r-lg);
    padding:14px 16px; box-shadow:var(--shadow);
  }
  .intro h2{ margin:0 0 2px; font:650 15px/1.25 var(--ui); display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px }
  .intro .letter{
    width:22px;height:22px;border-radius:6px;display:grid;place-items:center;flex:0 0 auto;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 26%, transparent);
    box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 45%, transparent);
    font:700 11px/1 var(--ui); color:#fff;
  }
  .intro .lede{ font-size:13px; color:var(--text-2); margin:6px 0 0 }
  .intro ul{ margin:0; padding-left:16px; font-size:12.5px; color:var(--text-2) }
  .intro ul li{ margin:2px 0 }
  .intro .tradeoff{
    margin-top:8px; padding:8px 10px; border-radius:8px;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--warning) 10%, transparent);
    border:1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--warning) 26%, transparent);
    font-size:12px; color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--warning) 82%, white);
  }
  .intro .tradeoff b{ color:var(--warning) }
  .intro h3{ margin:0 0 6px; font:600 10px/1 var(--ui); letter-spacing:.09em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--text-3) }

  /* ── chat canvas ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .canvas{
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--bg) 55%, var(--surface));
    border:1px solid var(--border-soft); border-radius:var(--r-lg);
    padding:12px 14px 18px; box-shadow:var(--shadow);
  }
  .msg{ border-radius:var(--r-md); padding:2px 4px 6px }
  .msg + .msg{ margin-top:2px }
  .msg.user{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 3%, transparent); padding:10px 12px }
  .msg.user .who-avatar{
    width:20px;height:20px;border-radius:50%;flex:0 0 auto;
    background:linear-gradient(140deg, var(--violet), var(--primary));
    display:grid;place-items:center;font:700 9px/1 var(--ui);color:#fff
  }
  .msg.user .row{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:7px }
  .msg.user .name{ font:600 12px/1 var(--ui) }
  .msg.user .time{ font-size:11px; color:var(--text-3); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums }
  .msg.user .txt{ margin:6px 0 0 27px; font-size:13.5px; color:var(--text-2) }

  /* header */
  .hdr{ position:relative; padding:2px 0 0 }
  .hdr-row{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; min-height:28px; flex-wrap:nowrap }
  .grow{ flex:1 1 auto; min-width:8px }

  /* identity cluster */
  .ident{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:7px; min-width:0 }
  .assistant-mark{
    width:20px;height:20px;border-radius:50%;flex:0 0 auto;
    background:linear-gradient(140deg, var(--primary), var(--secondary));
    display:grid;place-items:center;color:#fff;font:700 8px/1 var(--ui);
    box-shadow:0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 35%, transparent)
  }
  .who{ font:650 12.5px/1 var(--ui); color:var(--text) }
  .meta{ font-size:11px; color:var(--text-3); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:4px }
  .meta .i{ color:var(--text-3) }
  .sep{ width:1px; height:11px; background:var(--border); flex:0 0 auto }

  /* people (reaction / participant avatars) */
  .people{ display:flex; align-items:center; flex:0 0 auto }
  .people .av{
    width:19px;height:19px;border-radius:50%;margin-left:-5px;
    display:grid;place-items:center; font:700 8.5px/1 var(--ui); color:#fff;
    box-shadow:0 0 0 1.5px color-mix(in oklab, var(--bg) 55%, var(--surface));
    cursor:pointer; transition:transform var(--fast);
  }
  .people .av:first-child{ margin-left:0 }
  .people .av:hover{ transform:translateY(-1px) scale(1.06) }
  .av.p{ background:linear-gradient(140deg,#8B5CF6,#6D28D9) }
  .av.u{ background:linear-gradient(140deg,#3B82F6,#1D4ED8) }
  .av.e{ background:linear-gradient(140deg,#F59E0B,#F97316) }
  .av.r{ background:linear-gradient(140deg,#14B8A6,#0D9488) }

  /* ghost icon buttons */
  .ib{
    height:24px; min-width:24px; padding:0 5px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:5px;
    border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:7px; background:transparent;
    color:var(--text-3); cursor:pointer; transition:all var(--fast);
  }
  .ib:hover{ color:var(--text); background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 8%, transparent) }
  .ib:focus-visible{ outline:2px solid var(--primary); outline-offset:1px }
  .ib.on{ color:var(--primary-soft); background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 16%, transparent); border-color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 32%, transparent) }
  .ib.tool{ color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--info) 85%, white) }

  /* actions trigger */
  .act-trigger{
    height:26px; padding:0 7px 0 9px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px;
    border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:8px;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 4%, transparent);
    color:var(--text-2); font:550 11.5px/1 var(--ui); cursor:pointer;
    transition:all var(--fast); white-space:nowrap;
  }
  .act-trigger:hover{ color:var(--text); background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 9%, transparent) }
  .act-trigger[aria-expanded="true"]{
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 22%, transparent);
    border-color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 48%, transparent);
    color:var(--text);
    box-shadow:0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 12%, transparent);
  }
  .act-trigger .count{
    font:700 9.5px/1 var(--mono); padding:2px 4px; border-radius:4px;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 10%, transparent); color:var(--text-3);
  }
  .act-trigger[aria-expanded="true"] .count{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 45%, transparent); color:#fff }
  .act-trigger .i{ width:12px; height:12px; transition:transform var(--fast) }
  .act-trigger[aria-expanded="true"] .i.chev{ transform:rotate(180deg) }

  /* ── turn waterfall (unchanged, must stay visible) ───────────────────── */
  .tl-row{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:6px 1px 7px; border-top:1px solid var(--border-soft); margin-top:6px }
  .tl-track{
    flex:1 1 auto; height:13px; display:flex; align-items:stretch; gap:1px;
    padding:2px; border-radius:5px; background:var(--sunken);
    box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border-soft); overflow:hidden;
  }
  .sg{ border-radius:1.5px; min-width:1px; opacity:.85 }
  .sg.read{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--info) 62%, transparent) }
  .sg.web{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--violet) 62%, transparent) }
  .sg.exec{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--warning) 58%, transparent) }
  .sg.write{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--success) 55%, transparent) }
  .sg.agent{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 58%, transparent) }
  .sg.model{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 16%, transparent) }
  .sg.error{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--error) 78%, transparent); opacity:1 }
  .tl-count{
    flex:0 0 auto; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px;
    font:550 11px/1 var(--ui); color:var(--text-3); white-space:nowrap;
    font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;
  }
  .tl-count .err{ color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--error) 90%, white); font-weight:650 }
  .tl-count .i{ width:11px; height:11px }

  /* ── message body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .body{ font-size:13.5px; line-height:1.62; color:var(--text-2); padding:10px 1px 2px }
  .body p{ margin:0 0 7px }
  .body code{
    font:12px/1 var(--mono); padding:1.5px 4px; border-radius:4px;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 8%, transparent); color:var(--text)
  }
  .fade{
    position:relative; max-height:74px; overflow:hidden;
  }
  .fade::after{
    content:""; position:absolute; inset:auto 0 0 0; height:34px;
    background:linear-gradient(transparent, color-mix(in oklab, var(--bg) 55%, var(--surface)));
  }

  /* ── A / B: popover anchored to the HEADER, i.e. below the waterfall ── */
  .pop{
    position:absolute; right:2px; top:calc(100% + 8px); z-index:60;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--surface) 96%, transparent);
    border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:12px;
    box-shadow:0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.45), 0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
    backdrop-filter:blur(14px);
    animation:pop-in 140ms ease-out;
  }
  @keyframes pop-in{ from{ opacity:0; transform:translateY(-4px) } to{ opacity:1; transform:none } }
  .pop-head{
    display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:10px 10px 8px 12px;
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--border-soft);
  }
  .pop-head .t{ font:650 12px/1 var(--ui) }
  .pop-head .s{ font-size:10.5px; color:var(--text-3); margin-left:auto; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums }
  .pop-body{ padding:5px; max-height:min(52vh, 420px); overflow:auto }
  .pop-foot{
    display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:7px 10px;
    border-top:1px solid var(--border-soft); font:500 10.5px/1 var(--ui); color:var(--text-3);
  }
  .pop-foot .spacer{ flex:1 }

  .sec-label{
    padding:8px 8px 4px; font:600 9.5px/1 var(--ui);
    letter-spacing:.09em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--text-3);
  }
  .mi{
    width:100%; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:9px;
    height:30px; padding:0 8px; border:0; border-radius:7px;
    background:transparent; color:var(--text-2);
    font:500 12.5px/1 var(--ui); text-align:left; cursor:pointer;
    transition:background var(--fast), color var(--fast);
  }
  .mi .ic{ width:17px; display:grid; place-items:center; color:var(--text-3); transition:color var(--fast) }
  .mi .lbl{ flex:1; min-width:0; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap }
  .mi .tail{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:5px; flex:0 0 auto }
  .mi:hover, .mi.sel{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 15%, transparent); color:var(--text) }
  .mi:hover .ic, .mi.sel .ic{ color:var(--primary-soft) }
  .mi.on .lbl{ color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--success) 88%, white) }
  .mi.on .ic{ color:var(--success) }
  .mi.danger{ color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--error) 82%, white) }
  .mi.danger .ic{ color:var(--error) }
  .mi.danger:hover{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--error) 16%, transparent); color:var(--error) }
  .mi.danger:hover .ic{ color:var(--error) }
  .mi:focus-visible{ outline:2px solid var(--primary); outline-offset:-2px }
  .pop .hr{ height:1px; margin:5px 8px; background:var(--border-soft) }
  .check{ color:var(--success); width:12px; height:12px }

  /* footer chips (state toggles) */
  .foot-chips{ display:flex; gap:5px; padding:2px 5px 5px; flex-wrap:wrap }
  .fchip{
    display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px; height:24px; padding:0 8px;
    border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:var(--r-pill);
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 4%, transparent);
    color:var(--text-2); font:500 11px/1 var(--ui); cursor:pointer;
  }
  .fchip:hover{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 9%, transparent); color:var(--text) }
  .fchip.on{ color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--success) 88%, white); border-color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--success) 30%, transparent); background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--success) 12%, transparent) }
  .fchip .i{ width:11px; height:11px }

  /* ── A: width ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .pop-a{ width:296px }

  /* ── B: command palette ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .pop-b{ width:452px }
  .pal-search{
    display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:9px 10px;
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--border-soft);
  }
  .pal-search .i{ color:var(--text-3) }
  .pal-search input{
    flex:1; min-width:0; background:transparent; border:0; outline:none;
    color:var(--text); font:500 13px/1 var(--ui);
  }
  .pal-search input::placeholder{ color:var(--text-3) }
  .pal-cols{ display:grid; grid-template-columns:96px 1fr; min-height:0 }
  .pal-nav{ padding:6px 4px; border-right:1px solid var(--border-soft) }
  .pal-nav button{
    width:100%; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; height:26px; padding:0 7px;
    border:0; border-radius:6px; background:transparent; color:var(--text-3);
    font:500 11.5px/1 var(--ui); cursor:pointer; text-align:left;
  }
  .pal-nav button:hover{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 6%, transparent); color:var(--text-2) }
  .pal-nav button[aria-pressed="true"]{
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 20%, transparent); color:var(--text);
    box-shadow:inset 2px 0 0 var(--primary-soft)
  }
  .pal-nav .n{ margin-left:auto; font:600 9.5px/1 var(--mono); color:var(--text-3) }
  .pal-list{ padding:5px; overflow:auto; max-height:296px }

  /* ── C: inline toolbar, no overlay at all ────────────────────────────── */
  .toolbar{
    display:flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; flex-wrap:wrap;
    margin:4px 0 0; padding:7px 8px;
    border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:9px;
    background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 4%, transparent);
    animation:pop-in 140ms ease-out;
  }
  .toolbar .g{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:3px }
  .tb-div{ width:1px; height:16px; background:var(--border); margin:0 3px }
  .tb{
    display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px; height:25px; padding:0 8px;
    border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:6px; background:transparent;
    color:var(--text-2); font:500 11.5px/1 var(--ui); cursor:pointer;
    transition:all var(--fast); white-space:nowrap;
  }
  .tb .i{ width:12px; height:12px; color:var(--text-3) }
  .tb:hover{ background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 8%, transparent); color:var(--text) }

  // MOCK: a real turn comes from the events table; this is a fixed pattern so
  // the three variants can be compared pixel for pixel.
  function renderTrack(track){
    let s = 20251113;
    const rnd = () => ((s = (s * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7fffffff) / 0x7fffffff);
    const pool = ['read','read','read','read','web','web','exec','write','agent'];
    const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
    let count = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 138; i++) {
      // every 7th slot is model "thinking" (no tool call) → the hatched gaps
      const fam = (i % 7 === 3) ? 'model' : pool[Math.floor(rnd() * pool.length)];
      const el = document.createElement('span');
      el.className = 'sg ' + fam;
      el.style.flex = (fam === 'model' ? 1 + rnd() * 2.2 : 0.9 + rnd() * 2.6).toFixed(2);

      frag.appendChild(el);
      count++;
    }
    track.appendChild(frag);
  }
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-tl]').forEach(renderTrack);

  document.querySelectorAll('.act-trigger').forEach(btn => {

# Message header & actions — feature design

**Status:** proposal · design only, no product code changed
**Mockup:** [`01-mockup/index.html`](01-mockup/index.html) — three directions (A / B / C) behind a tab switch
**Touches:** `client/src/components/ChatEntry.vue` (header block + `⋯` dropdown), `client/src/components/chat/ChatTurnTimeline.vue` (row order only)

---

## 1. What the header is today

Verified in `ChatEntry.vue` (header block, lines ~56–310) and in the running product.

One 28 px row, `flex-wrap`, left-to-right:

| # | Control | Kind | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Archive box | **state change** | `$emit('hide')` |
| 2 | `13/Nov 09:15` | meta | `formatDate(updated_at)` |
| 3 | Clock (+ total) | meta | `time_taken` |
| 4 | `✓✓` | **toggle** | `toggleUnseenStatus` |
| 5 | Wrench / spinner | **toggle** (events panel) | `toggleEventsPanel` |
| 6 | Participant avatars | identity | `messageProfiles` |
| 7 | `⋯` | **menu** | 11 items |

then a second row: the turn waterfall (`ChatTurnTimeline`) and its `67 tools · 6m 09s ⌄` counter.

---

## 2. Defects found while designing (each one is fixed by the mockups)

**D1 — The `⋯` menu covers the waterfall it belongs to.**
`dropdown-content` opens downward from the kebab, which sits on the row directly above the bar.
Opening the menu hides the tool counter and the `⌄` expander — the two things a reader is most
likely to want next. *Seen in the supplied screenshot: the menu covers the right end of the bar.*

**D2 — Eleven items with no structure.**
`Thread · Mark as answer · Copy · Diff · Files · Review · Run agents · View source · Edit ·
Mark un-seen · Delete`. No group labels, no separators, no state marks (a toggle is only
distinguished by turning magenta), no shortcuts. `Delete` sits immediately below a benign toggle.

**D3 — The inline action row never renders.**
Every inline action uses `class="hidden @lg/panel:inline-flex …"`. In this Tailwind v4 build
`.hidden` wins over the container-query variant (measured in the previous iteration: `hidden +
@lg/panel:inline-flex` computes to `display:none` at every container width). Consequence: on a
wide panel the header still shows **only** the `⋯`, so the flat list is not a fallback — it is the
only entry point. Any redesign must assume that.

**D4 — Four different natures at one visual weight.**
State change, meta, toggle, identity and menu all render as ~11 px grey glyphs in the same
`gap-2` line, so the eye cannot classify them. `✓✓` (a receipt toggle) looks exactly like the
`⋯` (the menu).

**D5 — No keyboard story.**
The `<ul>` is `tabindex="0"` but the items are `<a>` without `role`, no roving focus, no
shortcuts, no `Esc` handling, and `Delete` is reachable by one `Tab` past `Edit`.

---

## 3. The three directions

All three keep the identity cluster, the state badges and the waterfall **unchanged**; only the
action surface differs, so the comparison is fair. Every one of them renders the actions
**below the waterfall row**, which is the hard requirement (D1).

### A — Grouped popover *(recommended default)*

Same trigger, organised content. The existing kebab stays, the list becomes four labelled
sections (**Reply · Copy · Inspect · Automate**) plus a footer that holds the two state chips
(`Seen`, `Archive`) and `Delete` on its own. Rows carry a shortcut on the right edge, active
toggles carry a `✓`, the popover has a title (`Message actions · Assistant · 09:15`) so a
screenshot of it is self-explaining.

* Why recommended: zero muscle-memory loss (one click, same place), fixes D1 and D2, and it is
  the only option that needs no new layout concept in `ChatEntry.vue` — the popover is anchored
  to the header block instead of to the button.
* Cost: popover is 296 px wide and covers the first two lines of the body while open.

### B — Action palette

The header keeps a single `Actions ⌘K` trigger; what opens is a filter field + category rail
(**All 11 · Reply 2 · Copy 3 · Inspect 5 · Automate 2 · Danger 1**) with counts, keyboard hints
and a footer that teaches `↑ ↓ ↵ esc`.

* Why: the only shape that still works at 25 actions, and it makes shortcuts discoverable.
* Cost: two clicks for Thread/Copy, ~450 × 400 px surface, and it presumes a shortcut layer the
  product does not have yet (`⌘K` must be claimed globally).

### C — Inline toolbar

No overlay. The actions expand **in place** as a labelled chip row inside the sticky header
(`Thread · Answer · Copy | Events & tools · Source · Diff · Files · Review PR | Run agents · Edit |
Un-seen · Archive · Delete`). The waterfall shifts down one row; nothing can ever be covered.

* Why: labels instead of guesses (`Review PR` reads; a branch glyph does not), zero occlusion,
  and it is the calmest option to screenshot for docs.
* Cost: +72 px of header height while open (measured, 13 chips, 2 rows at 1024 px), and it is
  visually louder than the current hover-only icon row.

---

## 4. Decision matrix

| | A popover | B palette | C toolbar |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Occludes the waterfall (D1) | ✅ no | ✅ no | ✅ no |
| Groups by intent (D2) | ✅ 4 sections | ✅ 5 categories | ✅ 3 groups |
| Clarity on wide panels (D3) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Visual hierarchy (D4) | ✅ identity / state / actions separated | ✅ best | ✅ |
| Keyboard (D5) | ✅ hints, needs wiring | ✅ best | ✅ tab order |
| Cost of first action | 1 click | 2 clicks | 1 click |
| Scales to ~25 actions | 🟡 scrolls | ✅ | ❌ wrapped |
| Layout risk in `ChatEntry.vue` | low | medium (new overlay) | low |
| Vertical cost while open | 0 | 0 (floats) | +72 px |

**Proposal:** ship **A** now (it fixes the three measurable defects and needs no new concept),
and keep **C** as the wide-panel form if the action list grows past ~12 — the two share the same
markup, A is C with the labels hidden.

---

## 5. Implementation sketch (option A)

1. **Anchor the popover to the header block**, not to the button: wrap
   `header-row + timeline-row` in a `position: relative` element and render the popover as an
   absolute child with `top: calc(100% + 8px); right: 0`. This is what removes D1 — the popover
   can no longer start above the waterfall.
2. **Replace the `<ul class="dropdown-content">`** with a `<div role="menu">` whose children are
   `<button role="menuitem">`, grouped by `<div role="group" aria-label="Reply">`. Keep the
   existing `@click.stop` handlers untouched.
3. **State marks:** `aria-checked` (or `aria-pressed`) on the three toggles — Knowledge answer,
   Diff/Files/Review — and render `✓` from that attribute instead of from `showDiff &&`.
4. **Footer:** `Seen` / `Archive` chips bound to `isMessageSeen` and `displayMessage.hide`;
   `Delete` stays `text-error` and is the only red item.
5. **Shortcuts** (`T C E S D F R P`): available only while the menu is open and no input has
   focus. Document them in the app's shortcut registry rather than hard-coding here.
6. **`.hidden` + `@lg/panel:inline-flex`**: replace with the inverse variant
   (`@max-lg/panel:hidden`) or drop the inline row for A entirely — the popover is sufficient at
   every width, which also removes D3.

---

## 6. Open questions

- Does the product already claim `⌘K`? If yes, B becomes the natural default.
- Should the header be **hover-only** for actions or always visible? Today it is always visible;
  all three mockups show it always visible for legibility at rest.
- `Seen` as a chip in the footer (A) versus an always-visible badge in the identity cluster
  (B, C). The badge is more honest — a receipt is state, not an action.
- Mobile (< 640 px): A's 296 px popover becomes a bottom sheet; C's chip row wraps to 4 rows and
  is probably too tall — the mockup collapses to one column below 820 px only to stay readable.

```md design/README.md
# codx-junior — Design Documentation

Corporate image and UI/UX foundation for **codx-junior**, derived from an audit of the
shipping product (`client/` — project `codx-junior-ui`).

> **Status:** v0.1 — *baseline definition*. Everything here describes either
> (a) what the product does **today**, verified in code, or (b) a **decision
> proposal** to close a gap. Each statement is labelled so the two never get
> confused.

> **Start here — [`playbook/index.html`](playbook/index.html).** The whole design system on
> one self-contained page: live component specimens, dark/light toggle, print-ready layout.
> Hand it to any developer before they write UI code.

---

## Why this folder exists

codx-junior grew feature-first: 400+ Vue components, several parallel shells
(desktop dockview, mobile app shell, company shell, solopreneur shell) and three
different colour palettes that leaked into the codebase over time. The product
works, but it does not yet look like *one company*.

This folder is the single place where the corporate image is defined, so that:

- a new screen can be designed without inventing new colours, spacing or copy;
- a designer and a developer can agree on a spec without a meeting;
- rebrand work (logo, palette, marketing site) has a contract to break *on purpose*.

---

## How to read it

| Folder | Contents | Audience |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `playbook/` | **The playbook** (`index.html`) — this whole folder on one page, with rendered specimens | Developers, new joiners |
| `resources/` | **Official artwork** — `logo.png` (the mark, 267 × 266 PNG + alpha) and `me-and-codx-junior.png` (brand photograph). Embedded by the playbook, taken from here, never re-exported | Everyone |
| `00-audit/` | What the current UI actually is, with file-level evidence | Designers, tech leads |
| `01-brand/` | Brand platform, logo, colour, typography, voice — the *corporate image* | Everyone, marketing included |
| `02-design-system/` | Foundations (space, radius, motion, layering) and component specs | Designers, frontend |
| `03-ux/` | Information architecture, navigation model, accessibility | Designers, PMs, frontend |
| `04-assets/` | Asset production rules: formats, sizes, naming, export | Design, marketing |
| `05-governance/` | Ownership, versioning, review checklist, adoption roadmap | Leads |
| `06-calendar/` | **Feature design** — agenda/calendar manager: deep analysis, clickable prototype, API fixtures. Design only, no code changed | Product, frontend, backend |
| `07-chat-timeline/` | **Feature design** — chat turn timeline (DevTools-style waterfall of a message's processing events) + insights rail. Clickable mockup, design only | Product, frontend, backend |
| `08-message-header/` | **Feature design** — chat message header + action menu: current anatomy, 5 measured defects, 3 directions (grouped popover / action palette / inline toolbar). Clickable mockup, design only | Product, frontend |
| `tokens/` | `design-tokens.json` — machine-readable source for the values above | Frontend |

Reading order for a newcomer: **audit → brand platform → colour → typography →
foundations → components → IA**.

---

## Ground rules

1. **The code is the current truth; this folder is the target truth.** When they
   disagree, the documents say which one wins.
2. **No new colour, radius or spacing value without a token.** If a value is
   missing, add a token here first, then use it.
3. **Every doc is versioned with the product**, not separately. See
   `05-governance/design-ops.md`.
4. **Numbers beat adjectives.** "16px, 8px grid, 4.5:1" is a spec; "modern and
   clean" is not.

---

## Source of truth (code references used throughout)

| Concern | File |
| --- | --- |
| Design tokens (live) | `client/src/assets/base.css` (Tailwind v4 + daisyUI 5) |
| Brand helper classes | `client/src/assets/main.css` (`--codx-primary` `#cc0099`, `--codx-secondary` `#8f008f`) |

Unified logging, event emission and cancellation for agent runs.
Wraps openai_ai without modifying it: openai_ai's stream/tool callbacks
are adapted onto AgentRunContext.

import json
import logging
import threading
import time
import uuid

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Iterator

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Errors

class AgentCancelled(Exception):
    """Raised at checkpoints when the run has been cancelled."""


class InsufficientFundsError(Exception):
    """Raised by the wallet pre-flight check."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Cancellation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class CancellationToken:
    """Thread-safe cancellation token. cancel() may be called from any thread
    (e.g. a Socket.IO 'stop' handler) while the agent loop runs elsewhere."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._event = threading.Event()
        self.reason: str | None = None

    def cancel(self, reason: str = "user_requested"):
        self.reason = reason
        self._event.set()

    @property
    def cancelled(self) -> bool:
        return self._event.is_set()

    def raise_if_cancelled(self):
        if self._event.is_set():
            raise AgentCancelled(self.reason or "cancelled")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Events
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class AgentEventType(str, Enum):
    RUN_START = "run_start"
    RUN_END = "run_end"
    RUN_ERROR = "run_error"
    RUN_CANCELLED = "run_cancelled"
    LLM_REQUEST = "llm_request"
    LLM_CHUNK = "llm_chunk"
    LLM_USAGE = "llm_usage"
    TOOL_START = "tool_start"
    TOOL_END = "tool_end"
    TOOL_ERROR = "tool_error"
    TOOL_LOGS = "tool_logs"
    WALLET_CHECK = "wallet_check"


@dataclass
class AgentEvent:
    type: AgentEventType
    run_id: str
    project_id: str
    payload: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"type": self.type.value, "run_id": self.run_id,
                "project_id": self.project_id, "ts": self.ts, **self.payload}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class RunAnalytics:
    prompt_tokens: int = 0
    completion_tokens: int = 0
    tool_calls: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # name -> {count, errors, total_ms}

    def on_event(self, event: AgentEvent):
        p = event.payload
        if event.type == AgentEventType.LLM_USAGE:
            self.prompt_tokens += p.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
            self.completion_tokens += p.get("completion_tokens", 0)
        elif event.type in (AgentEventType.TOOL_END, AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR):
            stats = self.tool_calls.setdefault(

            stats["count"] += 1
            stats["total_ms"] += p.get("duration_ms", 0.0)
            if event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR:
                stats["errors"] += 1

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        return {"prompt_tokens": self.prompt_tokens,
                "completion_tokens": self.completion_tokens,
                "total_tokens": self.prompt_tokens + self.completion_tokens,
                "tools": self.tool_calls}

def repair_incomplete_messages(
    chat: Any,
    chat_manager: Any,
    *,
    note: str = INTERRUPTED_NOTE,
    error: Optional[str] = None,
    hide: bool = True,
    skip_turn_ids: Optional[Any] = None,
) -> int:
    """
    Turn orphaned ``done=False`` assistant messages into a terminal state.

    These messages are the *"Processing request, please wait..."* placeholders
    persisted before the AI call. After a restart they would otherwise keep the
    client forever in the processing state and, worse, be rendered into the next
    prompt as a completed assistant answer.

    Args:
        chat: The chat to repair.
        chat_manager: Manager used to persist the repaired messages.
        note: Text appended to the interrupted message.
        error: Error recorded on the message (defaults to *note*).
        hide: Hide the message from the prompt/UI history (recommended).
        skip_turn_ids: Turn ids of LIVE turns; their in-flight messages must not
            be touched (e.g. a concurrent turn of the same chat).

    Returns:
        Number of messages repaired.
    """
    if chat is None:
        return 0

    skip = set(skip_turn_ids or ())
    repaired = 0
    for message in list(getattr(chat, "messages", []) or []):
        if getattr(message, "role", "") != "assistant":
            continue
        if getattr(message, "done", True) is not False:
            continue
        message_turn_id = str(
            (getattr(message, "meta_data", None) or {}).get("turn_id") or ""
        )
        if message_turn_id and message_turn_id in skip:
            continue

        content = str(getattr(message, "content", "") or "")
        if note and note.strip() not in content:
            content = (content.rstrip() + note) if content.strip() else note.strip()
        elif not note and "processing request" in content.lower():
            # Replace the placeholder with a terminal note: the client may not
            # filter ``hide`` locally, and "processing" must never survive.
            content = f"*({error or 'The turn was interrupted'})*"
        message.content = content
        message.done = True
        message.error = message.error or error or "The turn was interrupted"
        message.meta_data = {
            **(getattr(message, "meta_data", None) or {}),
            "interrupted": True,
            "interrupted_at": _now(),
        }
        message.hide = bool(hide)

        try:
            update = getattr(chat_manager, "update_message", None)
            if callable(update):
                update(chat=chat, message=message)
            else:  # pragma: no cover - defensive fallback
                chat_manager.save_chat(chat=chat)
            repaired += 1
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.warning(
                "ChatTurnStore: could not persist repaired message '%s': %s",
                getattr(message, "doc_id", ""),
                ex,
            )
    if repaired:
        logger.info(
            "ChatTurnStore: repaired %d interrupted response message(s) of "
            "chat '%s'",
            repaired,
            getattr(chat, "id", ""),
        )
    return repaired

"""
ChatEventBridge — attaches AgentRunContext events to the chat response message
and persists it on EVERY change (crash-safe).

During an AI turn the SmolAgent emits :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentEvent`
notifications (tool start/end/error, run lifecycle).

Events are ASSOCIATED with the assistant **response message** that the
ChatEngine created BEFORE calling the AI — they are never emitted as separate
chat messages:

    * ``response_message.tool_events``      → list of :class:`ToolEvent`
      (one entry per tool call, updated in place: running → done/error). Each
      event also carries the tool's user-facing ``output`` so tool output can be
      rendered collapsed/hidden instead of polluting ``Message.content``.
    * ``response_message.lifecycle_events`` → list of :class:`LifeCycleEvent`
      (one entry per agent run, updated in place)

Tool output
-----------
TOOL_END events carry the dual-response tool's user-facing ``output``
(``ToolResponse.user_response``). The bridge stores it on the matching
:class:`ToolEvent` (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of it being merged into the
chat content, so the client decides how to display it. Cached tool calls do not
re-emit output (the first execution already delivered it).

Crash-safety guarantee
----------------------
On every event change the response message is:

    1. **Persisted immediately** via the ChatManager granular merge-safe
       methods (``add_message`` on first change, ``update_message`` after).
       If the process dies mid-run, every event received so far — including
       tool errors, run errors and aggregated analytics — is already on disk.
    2. **Streamed** to clients in real time via the EventManager so the UI
       can render tool progress live.

ADDED — streamed-chunk crash-safety (:meth:`maybe_persist_stream`):
    Streaming callbacks may call :meth:`maybe_persist_stream` on every flush;
    the bridge persists the response message AT MOST once per
    ``STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` (monotonic clock). A hard kill
    therefore loses at most that many seconds of streamed partial text while
    keeping disk I/O bounded.

    def _progress(self) -> None:

        *min_interval_seconds* (measured with a monotonic clock across ALL
        persists, including event-driven ones). This bounds disk I/O while
        guaranteeing a hard kill loses at most *min_interval_seconds* of

                self.chat.id,

                    "chat_manager for chat '%s' — message '%s' NOT persisted",
                    self.chat.id,

                "chat '%s' (message '%s')",

                "ChatEventBridge: fallback save_chat failed for chat '%s': %s",
                self.chat.id,
                ex,
            )

        """Stream the current response message state to clients (never raises)."""
        try:

----------------------

            # lost. Cached tool calls do not carry an output (see SmolAgent).
            output = payload.get("output")
            if output:
                tool_event.output = str(output)

            "ChatEventBridge: tool '%s' %s in %.0f ms (chat='%s')",
            tool_event.tool,
            tool_event.status,
            duration_ms,
            self.chat.id,
        )
        self.publish()

    # ── Lifecycle events ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _on_lifecycle(self, event: AgentEvent) -> None:
        """
        Update (in place) the LifeCycleEvent of this run, then persist + stream.

        One LifeCycleEvent is kept per ``run_id``; recursive agent iterations
        that reuse the same bridge get one entry per run. RUN_ERROR /
        RUN_CANCELLED details are persisted the moment they arrive so no
        failure information is lost on a subsequent crash.
        """
        payload = event.payload
        lifecycle_event = self._lifecycle_events.get(event.run_id)
        if lifecycle_event is None:
            lifecycle_event = LifeCycleEvent(
                status=STATUS_RUNNING,
                run_id=event.run_id,
            )
            self._lifecycle_events[event.run_id] = lifecycle_event
            self.response_message.lifecycle_events.append(lifecycle_event)

        if event.type == AgentEventType.RUN_END:
            lifecycle_event.status = STATUS_DONE
            lifecycle_event.duration_ms = payload.get("duration_ms")
        elif event.type in (AgentEventType.RUN_ERROR, AgentEventType.RUN_CANCELLED):
            lifecycle_event.status = STATUS_ERROR
            lifecycle_event.duration_ms = payload.get("duration_ms")
            lifecycle_event.error = str(
                payload.get("error") or payload.get("reason") or "unknown error"
            )

        analytics = payload.get("analytics")
        if analytics is not None:
            meta = dict(self.response_message.meta_data or {})
            meta["analytics"] = analytics
            self.response_message.meta_data = meta

        logger.info(
            "ChatEventBridge: lifecycle '%s' status=%s (chat='%s', run='%s')",
            event.type,
            lifecycle_event.status,
            self.chat.id,
            event.run_id,
        )

    def publish(self) -> None:
        """
        Persist the response message (crash-safe) and stream it to clients.

        Persistence is idempotent by ``doc_id``: the first call inserts the
        message via ``add_message``, subsequent calls update it in place via
        ``update_message``. The ChatEngine also calls this method on its own
        error / cancellation paths so failure information is written to disk
        the moment it is known.
        """
        self._persist_message(self.response_message)
        self._stream()

    def persist_message(self, message: Message) -> None:
        """

        Used by the engine to persist hidden reasoning messages (and any other
        mid-run message) the moment they are produced instead of waiting for
        the end-of-turn chat save. Idempotent by ``doc_id`` and never raises.

        :param message: The auxiliary Message to persist immediately.
        """
        self._persist_message(message)

    def maybe_persist_stream(
        self,
        min_interval_seconds: float = STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
    ) -> bool:
        """

        Intended to be called from streaming callbacks on every flush; the
        response message is written to disk AT MOST once per
        *min_interval_seconds* (measured with a monotonic clock across ALL
        persists, including event-driven ones). This bounds disk I/O while
        guaranteeing a hard kill loses at most *min_interval_seconds* of
        streamed partial text. Never raises.

        :param min_interval_seconds: Minimum seconds between persists.
        :return: True if a persist was performed, False if throttled.
        """
        now = time.monotonic()
        if now - self._last_persist_ts < min_interval_seconds:
            return False
        logger.debug(
            "ChatEventBridge: throttled stream persist for chat '%s'",
            self.chat.id,
        )
        self._persist_message(self.response_message)
        # Persisted content is progress: refresh the turn heartbeat.
        self._progress()
        return True

    def _persist_message(self, message: Message) -> None:
        """
        Write *message* to disk idempotently (never raises).

        Uses the granular merge-safe ChatManager methods when available.
        DEFENSIVE: if the manager lacks ``add_message`` / ``update_message``
        or they fail, falls back to :meth:`_fallback_save_chat` so no
        information is silently dropped.

        :param message: The message (response or auxiliary) to persist.
        """
        try:
            if message.doc_id not in self._persisted_doc_ids:
                self.chat_manager.add_message(chat=self.chat, message=message)
                self._persisted_doc_ids.add(message.doc_id)
            else:
                self.chat_manager.update_message(chat=self.chat, message=message)
            self._last_persist_ts = time.monotonic()
        except AttributeError as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "ChatEventBridge: chat_manager lacks granular persistence "
                "(add_message/update_message): %s — falling back to full "
                "chat save for message '%s' (chat '%s')",
                ex,
                message.doc_id,
                self.chat.id,
            )
            self._fallback_save_chat(message)
        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as ex:
            logger.exception(
                "ChatEventBridge: error persisting message '%s' for chat "
                "'%s': %s — attempting full chat save fallback",
                message.doc_id,
                self.chat.id,
                ex,
            )
            self._fallback_save_chat(message)

    def _fallback_save_chat(self, message: Message) -> None:
        """
        DEFENSIVE fallback: persist the full chat via ``save_chat``.

        Ensures *message* is present on the in-memory chat before the coarse
        write so the fallback still captures it. Never raises.

        :param message: The message that triggered the fallback.
        """
        try:
            save_chat = getattr(self.chat_manager, "save_chat", None)
            if save_chat is None:
                logger.error(
                    "ChatEventBridge: no persistence method available on "
                    "chat_manager for chat '%s' — message '%s' NOT persisted",
                    self.chat.id,
                    message.doc_id,
                )
                return
            if not any(m.doc_id == message.doc_id for m in self.chat.messages):
                self.chat.messages.append(message)
            save_chat(chat=self.chat)
            self._persisted_doc_ids.add(message.doc_id)
            self._last_persist_ts = time.monotonic()
            logger.info(
                "ChatEventBridge: fallback full chat save succeeded for "
                "chat '%s' (message '%s')",
                self.chat.id,
                message.doc_id,
            )
        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as ex:
            logger.exception(
                "ChatEventBridge: fallback save_chat failed for chat '%s': %s",
                self.chat.id,
                ex,
            )

    def _stream(self) -> None:
        """Stream the current response message state to clients (never raises)."""
        try:
            self.event_manager.message_event(
                chat=self.chat, message=self.response_message
            )
        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as ex:
            logger.exception(
                "ChatEventBridge: error streaming response message '%s' "
                "for chat '%s': %s",
                self.response_message.doc_id,
                self.chat.id,
                ex,
            )

"""
ChatEventBridge — attaches AgentRunContext events to the chat response message
and persists it on EVERY change (crash-safe).

During an AI turn the SmolAgent emits :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentEvent`
notifications (tool start/end/error, run lifecycle).

Events are ASSOCIATED with the assistant **response message** that the
ChatEngine created BEFORE calling the AI — they are never emitted as separate
chat messages:

    * ``response_message.tool_events``      → list of :class:`ToolEvent`
      (one entry per tool call, updated in place: running → done/error). Each
      event also carries the tool's user-facing ``output`` so tool output can be
      rendered collapsed/hidden instead of polluting ``Message.content``.
    * ``response_message.lifecycle_events`` → list of :class:`LifeCycleEvent`
      (one entry per agent run, updated in place)

Tool output
-----------
TOOL_END events carry the dual-response tool's user-facing ``output``
(``ToolResponse.user_response``). The bridge stores it on the matching
:class:`ToolEvent` (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of it being merged into the
chat content, so the client decides how to display it. Cached tool calls do not
re-emit output (the first execution already delivered it).

Crash-safety guarantee
----------------------
On every event change the response message is:

    1. **Persisted immediately** via the ChatManager granular merge-safe
       methods (``add_message`` on first change, ``update_message`` after).
       If the process dies mid-run, every event received so far — including
       tool errors, run errors and aggregated analytics — is already on disk.
    2. **Streamed** to clients in real time via the EventManager so the UI
       can render tool progress live.

ADDED — streamed-chunk crash-safety (:meth:`maybe_persist_stream`):
    Streaming callbacks may call :meth:`maybe_persist_stream` on every flush;
    the bridge persists the response message AT MOST once per
    ``STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` (monotonic clock). A hard kill
    therefore loses at most that many seconds of streamed partial text while
    keeping disk I/O bounded.

ADDED — auxiliary message crash-safety (:meth:`persist_message`):
    Any auxiliary message produced mid-run (e.g. hidden reasoning messages)
    can be persisted immediately and idempotently. Persisted ``doc_id``s are
    tracked bridge-side so the first call inserts (``add_message``) and later
    calls update (``update_message``).

ADDED — defensive ChatManager fallback:
    The idempotency guarantee assumes ``ChatManager.update_message`` matches
    by ``doc_id``. If the granular methods are missing or fail, the bridge
    falls back to a coarse ``save_chat`` full write (after making sure the
    message is on the in-memory chat) so information is never silently lost.

The engine reuses :meth:`publish` on its own error / cancellation paths so
``response_message.error`` and ``cancelled_at`` are also persisted the moment
they are known, not only at the end of the turn.

    crash-safe persistence on every change.

    :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext` and must **never raise**:

        chat_manager,

        :param event_manager: EventManager used to stream message events.

        # every event and on every persisted streaming flush, so the recovery
        # worker can tell a SLOW turn from a DEAD one (no progress) and restart
        # the execution instead of leaving the chat on "processing" forever.
        self.progress_callback = progress_callback

        # covers the response message AND any auxiliary message).
        self._persisted_doc_ids: Set[str] = set()

            elif event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_END:

                "ChatEventBridge: failed handling event '%s' for chat '%s': %s",
                event.type,

            tool=payload.get("tool", "unknown"),

            status=status,

        :param message: The auxiliary Message to persist immediately.

        self._persist_message(message)

    def maybe_persist_stream(
        self,
        min_interval_seconds: float = STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        ADDED: Throttled persist of the response message for streamed content.

        Intended to be called from streaming callbacks on every flush; the
        response message is written to disk AT MOST once per
        *min_interval_seconds* (measured with a monotonic clock across ALL
        persists, including event-driven ones). This bounds disk I/O while
        guaranteeing a hard kill loses at most *min_interval_seconds* of
        streamed partial text. Never raises.

        :return: True if a persist was performed, False if throttled.

            return False

            "ChatEventBridge: throttled stream persist for chat '%s'",
            self.chat.id,

                "ChatEventBridge: chat_manager lacks granular persistence "

                "chat save for message '%s' (chat '%s')",

        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as ex:
            logger.exception(
                "ChatEventBridge: error persisting message '%s' for chat "

                message.doc_id,

                ex,

                "chat '%s' (message '%s')",
                self.chat.id,
                message.doc_id,

            logger.exception(
                "ChatEventBridge: fallback save_chat failed for chat '%s': %s",
                self.chat.id,
                ex,
            )

        """Stream the current response message state to clients (never raises)."""
        try:
            self.event_manager.message_event(
                chat=self.chat, message=self.response_message

                "ChatEventBridge: error streaming response message '%s' "
                "for chat '%s': %s",
                self.response_message.doc_id,
                self.chat.id,

"""
ChatEventBridge — attaches AgentRunContext events to the chat response message
and persists it on EVERY change (crash-safe).

During an AI turn the SmolAgent emits :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentEvent`
notifications (tool start/end/error, run lifecycle).

Events are ASSOCIATED with the assistant **response message** that the
ChatEngine created BEFORE calling the AI — they are never emitted as separate
chat messages:

    * ``response_message.tool_events``      → list of :class:`ToolEvent`
      (one entry per tool call, updated in place: running → done/error). Each
      event also carries the tool's user-facing ``output`` so tool output can be
      rendered collapsed/hidden instead of polluting ``Message.content``.
    * ``response_message.lifecycle_events`` → list of :class:`LifeCycleEvent`
      (one entry per agent run, updated in place)

Tool output
-----------
TOOL_END events carry the dual-response tool's user-facing ``output``
(``ToolResponse.user_response``). The bridge stores it on the matching
:class:`ToolEvent` (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of it being merged into the
chat content, so the client decides how to display it. Cached tool calls do not
re-emit output (the first execution already delivered it).

Crash-safety guarantee
----------------------
On every event change the response message is:

    1. **Persisted immediately** via the ChatManager granular merge-safe
       methods (``add_message`` on first change, ``update_message`` after).
       If the process dies mid-run, every event received so far — including
       tool errors, run errors and aggregated analytics — is already on disk.
    2. **Streamed** to clients in real time via the EventManager so the UI
       can render tool progress live.

ADDED — streamed-chunk crash-safety (:meth:`maybe_persist_stream`):
    Streaming callbacks may call :meth:`maybe_persist_stream` on every flush;
    the bridge persists the response message AT MOST once per
    ``STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` (monotonic clock). A hard kill
    therefore loses at most that many seconds of streamed partial text while
    keeping disk I/O bounded.

ADDED — auxiliary message crash-safety (:meth:`persist_message`):
    Any auxiliary message produced mid-run (e.g. hidden reasoning messages)
    can be persisted immediately and idempotently. Persisted ``doc_id``s are
    tracked bridge-side so the first call inserts (``add_message``) and later
    calls update (``update_message``).

ADDED — defensive ChatManager fallback:
    The idempotency guarantee assumes ``ChatManager.update_message`` matches
    by ``doc_id``. If the granular methods are missing or fail, the bridge
    falls back to a coarse ``save_chat`` full write (after making sure the
    message is on the in-memory chat) so information is never silently lost.

The engine reuses :meth:`publish` on its own error / cancellation paths so
``response_message.error`` and ``cancelled_at`` are also persisted the moment
they are known, not only at the end of the turn.

def _truncate(text: str, max_chars: int = TOOL_RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS) -> str:
    """
    Truncate *text* to *max_chars*, appending an ellipsis marker when cut.

    :param text: The text to truncate.
    :param max_chars: Maximum number of characters to keep.
    :return: The (possibly truncated) text.
    """

class ChatEventBridge:
    """
    Bridges agent runtime events onto the chat RESPONSE message with
    crash-safe persistence on every change.

    The bridge is registered as a listener on an
    :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext` and must **never raise**:
    any persistence/streaming failure is logged and swallowed so a broken
    notification can never kill the AI run.

    All events are stored as typed entries on the response message
    (``tool_events`` / ``lifecycle_events``). The message reference is shared
    with the ChatEngine, so mutations are visible immediately.

    Persistence idempotency is enforced BRIDGE-SIDE: the bridge tracks which
    ``doc_id``s have already been inserted and calls ``add_message`` only
    once per message, then ``update_message`` afterwards. If the ChatManager
    lacks these granular methods (or they fail), the bridge falls back to a
    coarse ``save_chat`` full write so no information is dropped.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        chat: Chat,
        response_message: Message,
        chat_manager,
        event_manager,
        progress_callback=None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        :param chat: The in-memory chat being processed (shared reference).
        :param response_message: The assistant response message created by the
                                 ChatEngine BEFORE the AI call; events are
                                 attached to it (mutated in place).
        :param chat_manager: ChatManager providing merge-safe
                             ``add_message`` / ``update_message`` persistence
                             (``save_chat`` used as a defensive fallback).
        :param event_manager: EventManager used to stream message events.
        """
        self.chat: Chat = chat
        self.response_message: Message = response_message
        self.chat_manager = chat_manager
        self.event_manager = event_manager
        # Progress heartbeat of the durable turn record (optional). Called on
        # every event and on every persisted streaming flush, so the recovery
        # worker can tell a SLOW turn from a DEAD one (no progress) and restart
        # the execution instead of leaving the chat on "processing" forever.
        self.progress_callback = progress_callback
        # ADDED: doc_ids already inserted on disk (idempotency enforced here,
        # covers the response message AND any auxiliary message).
        self._persisted_doc_ids: Set[str] = set()
        # ADDED: monotonic timestamp of the last successful persist; primed to
        # "now" so the initial "Processing..." placeholder is not persisted
        # immediately — the first throttled persist happens after the interval.
        self._last_persist_ts: float = time.monotonic()
        # tool_call_id (or tool name fallback) -> in-place updated ToolEvent
        self._tool_events: Dict[str, ToolEvent] = {}
        # run_id -> in-place updated LifeCycleEvent
        self._lifecycle_events: Dict[str, LifeCycleEvent] = {}

    @property
    def response_persisted(self) -> bool:
        """True when the response message has already been inserted on disk."""
        return self.response_message.doc_id in self._persisted_doc_ids

    # ── Progress heartbeat ─────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _progress(self) -> None:
        """
        Report PROGRESS to the turn heartbeat (never raises).

        A turn that stops reporting progress stopped working: the recovery
        worker sees the stale heartbeat, stops it and restarts the execution.
        """
        if self.progress_callback is None:
            return
        try:
            self.progress_callback()
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - a heartbeat never kills a run
            logger.debug(
                "ChatEventBridge: progress callback failed for chat '%s': %s",
                self.chat.id,
                ex,
            )

    # ── Event entry point ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def on_event(self, event: AgentEvent) -> None:
        """
        Handle an :class:`AgentEvent` emitted by the agent run context.

        :param event: The emitted event.
        """
        try:
            if event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_START:
                self._on_tool_start(event)
            elif event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_END:
                self._on_tool_finished(event, error=False)
            elif event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR:
                self._on_tool_finished(event, error=True)
            elif event.type in LIFECYCLE_EVENT_TYPES:
                self._on_lifecycle(event)
        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as ex:
            # A broken notification must NEVER kill the AI run.
            logger.exception(
                "ChatEventBridge: failed handling event '%s' for chat '%s': %s",
                event.type,
                self.chat.id,
                ex,
            )
        finally:
            # Every handled event is PROGRESS of the run.
            self._progress()

    # ── Tool events ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @staticmethod
    def _tool_key(event: AgentEvent) -> str:
        """Return the lookup key for the tool event of *event*."""
        return str(event.payload.get("tool_call_id") or event.payload.get("tool") or "")

    def _register_tool_event(self, event: AgentEvent, status: str) -> ToolEvent:
        """
        Create a new ToolEvent, attach it to the response message and track it.

        :param event: The originating TOOL_* agent event.
        :param status: Initial status ('running', 'done', or 'error').
        :return: The registered ToolEvent instance.
        """
        payload = event.payload
        tool_event = ToolEvent(
            tool=payload.get("tool", "unknown"),
            tool_call_id=str(payload.get("tool_call_id") or ""),
            status=status,
            request=payload.get("args") or {},
        )
        self._tool_events[self._tool_key(event)] = tool_event
        self.response_message.tool_events.append(tool_event)
        return tool_event

    def _on_tool_start(self, event: AgentEvent) -> None:
        """Attach a new 'running' ToolEvent, then persist + stream immediately."""
        tool_event = self._register_tool_event(event, status=STATUS_RUNNING)
        logger.info(
            "ChatEventBridge: tool '%s' started (chat='%s', run='%s')",
            tool_event.tool,
            self.chat.id,
            event.run_id,
        )
        self.publish()

    def _on_tool_finished(self, event: AgentEvent, error: bool) -> None:
        """Update the matching ToolEvent in place, then persist + stream."""
        payload = event.payload
        duration_ms = payload.get("duration_ms", 0.0) or 0.0

        tool_event = self._tool_events.get(self._tool_key(event))
        if tool_event is None:
            # Defensive: TOOL_END/TOOL_ERROR without a matching TOOL_START
            tool_event = self._register_tool_event(event, status=STATUS_RUNNING)

        tool_event.duration_ms = duration_ms

        if error:
            tool_event.status = STATUS_ERROR
            tool_event.error = _truncate(str(payload.get("error") or "unknown error"))
        else:
            tool_event.status = STATUS_DONE
            tool_event.response = _truncate(str(payload.get("result") or ""))
            # Tool output (dual-response user_response) is attached as a
            # collapsible message property instead of being merged into the
            # chat content. Stored UNTRUNCATED so generated code/blocks are not
            # lost. Cached tool calls do not carry an output (see SmolAgent).
            output = payload.get("output")
            if output:
                tool_event.output = str(output)

        logger.info(
            "ChatEventBridge: tool '%s' %s in %.0f ms (chat='%s')",
            tool_event.tool,
            tool_event.status,
            duration_ms,
            self.chat.id,
        )
        self.publish()

    # ── Lifecycle events ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _on_lifecycle(self, event: AgentEvent) -> None:
        """
        Update (in place) the LifeCycleEvent of this run, then persist + stream.

        One LifeCycleEvent is kept per ``run_id``; recursive agent iterations
        that reuse the same bridge get one entry per run. RUN_ERROR /
        RUN_CANCELLED details are persisted the moment they arrive so no
        failure information is lost on a subsequent crash.
        """
        payload = event.payload
        lifecycle_event = self._lifecycle_events.get(event.run_id)
        if lifecycle_event is None:
            lifecycle_event = LifeCycleEvent(
                status=STATUS_RUNNING,
                run_id=event.run_id,
            )
            self._lifecycle_events[event.run_id] = lifecycle_event
            self.response_message.lifecycle_events.append(lifecycle_event)

        if event.type == AgentEventType.RUN_END:
            lifecycle_event.status = STATUS_DONE
            lifecycle_event.duration_ms = payload.get("duration_ms")
        elif event.type in (AgentEventType.RUN_ERROR, AgentEventType.RUN_CANCELLED):
            lifecycle_event.status = STATUS_ERROR
            lifecycle_event.duration_ms = payload.get("duration_ms")
            lifecycle_event.error = str(
                payload.get("error") or payload.get("reason") or "unknown error"
            )

        # Aggregated run analytics are supplementary metadata on the response.
        analytics = payload.get("analytics")
        if analytics is not None:
            meta = dict(self.response_message.meta_data or {})
            meta["analytics"] = analytics
            self.response_message.meta_data = meta

        logger.info(
            "ChatEventBridge: lifecycle '%s' status=%s (chat='%s', run='%s')",
            event.type,
            lifecycle_event.status,
            self.chat.id,
            event.run_id,
        )
        self.publish()

    # ── Persist + stream ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def publish(self) -> None:
        """
        Persist the response message (crash-safe) and stream it to clients.

        Persistence is idempotent by ``doc_id``: the first call inserts the
        message via ``add_message``, subsequent calls update it in place via
        ``update_message``. The ChatEngine also calls this method on its own
        error / cancellation paths so failure information is written to disk
        the moment it is known.
        """
        self._persist_message(self.response_message)
        self._stream()

    def persist_message(self, message: Message) -> None:
        """
        ADDED: Crash-safe persistence of an AUXILIARY message.

        Used by the engine to persist hidden reasoning messages (and any other
        mid-run message) the moment they are produced instead of waiting for
        the end-of-turn chat save. Idempotent by ``doc_id`` and never raises.

        :param message: The auxiliary Message to persist immediately.
        """
        self._persist_message(message)

    def maybe_persist_stream(
        self,
        min_interval_seconds: float = STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        ADDED: Throttled persist of the response message for streamed content.

        Intended to be called from streaming callbacks on every flush; the
        response message is written to disk AT MOST once per
        *min_interval_seconds* (measured with a monotonic clock across ALL
        persists, including event-driven ones). This bounds disk I/O while
        guaranteeing a hard kill loses at most *min_interval_seconds* of
        streamed partial text. Never raises.

        :param min_interval_seconds: Minimum seconds between persists.
        :return: True if a persist was performed, False if throttled.
        """
        now = time.monotonic()
        if now - self._last_persist_ts < min_interval_seconds:
            return False
        logger.debug(
            "ChatEventBridge: throttled stream persist for chat '%s'",
            self.chat.id,
        )
        self._persist_message(self.response_message)
        # Persisted content is progress: refresh the turn heartbeat.
        self._progress()
        return True

    def _persist_message(self, message: Message) -> None:
        """
        Write *message* to disk idempotently (never raises).

        Uses the granular merge-safe ChatManager methods when available.
        DEFENSIVE: if the manager lacks ``add_message`` / ``update_message``
        or they fail, falls back to :meth:`_fallback_save_chat` so no
        information is silently dropped.

        :param message: The message (response or auxiliary) to persist.
        """
        try:
            if message.doc_id not in self._persisted_doc_ids:
                self.chat_manager.add_message(chat=self.chat, message=message)
                self._persisted_doc_ids.add(message.doc_id)
            else:
                self.chat_manager.update_message(chat=self.chat, message=message)
            self._last_persist_ts = time.monotonic()
        except AttributeError as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "ChatEventBridge: chat_manager lacks granular persistence "
                "(add_message/update_message): %s — falling back to full "
                "chat save for message '%s' (chat '%s')",
